traceability.evidence:
Story file: - docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md exists and defines detailed requirements for file existence checks, path resolution via context.cwd, security (no traversal/absolute paths outside project), configurable story directories, caching, and clear error messages.
Core implementation: - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - Rule description: "Validate that @story annotations reference existing .story.md files". - Parses comments and extracts @story lines (handleComment, validateStoryPath), satisfying REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION. - Uses (context as any).cwd ?? process.cwd() as the base, then passes this cwd plus configured storyDirectories into normalizeStoryPath, meeting the story's requirement to resolve relative to project root/context.cwd (REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION). - Security: - Rejects absolute paths with invalidPath when allowAbsolutePaths is false; when allowed, they still go through extension and boundary checks (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). - Detects traversal (.. segments) with containsPathTraversal and rejects if the normalized resolved path escapes cwd, reporting invalidPath (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). - Extension: - When requireStoryExtension is true, uses hasValidExtension (".story.md") and reports invalidExtension otherwise (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION and acceptance criteria for .story.md naming). - Existence & project boundary: - Calls normalizeStoryPath(...).existence and candidates. - handleProjectBoundaryForExistence uses enforceProjectBoundary on all candidates and any matchedPath to ensure they remain within project root; if not, reports invalidPath (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - reportExistenceStatus distinguishes between: * status === "missing" -> fileMissing. * status === "fs-error" -> fileAccessError including a normalized error message (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING). - Configuration: - meta.schema exposes options: storyDirectories (array of strings), allowAbsolutePaths (boolean), requireStoryExtension (boolean) (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - Defaults: storyDirectories = ["docs/stories", "stories"], allowAbsolutePaths = false, requireStoryExtension = true. - User messaging: - meta.messages defines fileMissing, invalidExtension, invalidPath, fileAccessError with clear, specific templates including {{path}} and {{error}}, satisfying the User Experience and Error Handling acceptance criteria.
Utility implementation: - src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts - buildStoryCandidates(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs): - For "./" or "../" paths: resolves only against cwd. - For bare paths: resolves cwd + storyPath, then cwd + each storyDirectories entry + basename(storyPath) (REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - enforceProjectBoundary(candidate, cwd): - Normalizes both paths and ensures candidate is equal to or under cwd, returning { candidate, isWithinProject }, used by the rule to enforce project boundaries (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - Existence & caching: - fileExistStatusCache: Map caches fs checks (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION). - checkSingleCandidate: * Wraps fs.existsSync and fs.statSync in try/catch, never throws. * Distinguishes "exists" (regular file), "missing", and "fs-error" with captured error (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION). - getStoryExistence(candidates): * Returns first "exists" as matchedPath. * If none exist but at least one fs-error occurred, returns status "fs-error" with that error; otherwise returns "missing" (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING). - storyExists(paths): uses getStoryExistence and returns a boolean without throwing (backwards-compatible, still honoring robust error handling). - __resetStoryExistenceCacheForTests(): allows tests to reset cache between scenarios (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION testability). - Security helpers: isAbsolutePath, containsPathTraversal, isTraversalUnsafe, hasValidExtension, isUnsafeStoryPath implement the security and extension constraints (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION).
Tests for this story: - tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts - Header explicitly references this story: - "Tests for: docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md" and @story/@req tags aligning with the story requirements. - RuleTester suite: "Valid Story Reference Rule (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)" tests core behavior: - Valid cases: * [REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE] valid .story.md path under docs/stories. * [REQ-EXTENSION] valid .story.md extension. * [REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION] relative path with ./ prefix. - Invalid cases: * Missing file: expects messageId "fileMissing" with the original path (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, User Experience). * Wrong extension: expects "invalidExtension" (extension validation & messaging). * Path traversal ("../outside.story.md"): expects "invalidPath" (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). * Absolute path "/etc/passwd.story.md" with default config: expects "invalidPath" (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). - Additional RuleTester groups validate configurability and boundaries (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY): - configurablePathsTester: * Uses options { storyDirectories: ["docs/stories"] } and verifies that a bare story filename plus a fully qualified docs/stories path are both accepted. - allowAbsolutePathsTester: * Valid: allowAbsolutePaths: true with an existing absolute path inside project and docs/stories in storyDirectories. * Invalid: the same path but allowAbsolutePaths: false -> invalidPath. - relaxedExtensionTester: * Options { storyDirectories: ["docs/stories"], requireStoryExtension: false }. * Ensures no invalidExtension diagnostic for a .story.md path when extension enforcement is disabled, confirming behavior of requireStoryExtension. - projectBoundaryTester: * Configures allowAbsolutePaths: true and storyDirectories pointing to an outside-project absolute directory (e.g., "/outside-project"). * Code uses a story path from that outside-project directory, plus a valid internal story. * Expects invalidPath, proving that even with misconfigured storyDirectories and absolute paths enabled, references outside project root are rejected (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - Jest-based tests: "Valid Story Reference Rule Configuration and Boundaries (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)" and "Valid Story Reference Rule Error Handling (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)" further validate: - Resolution via storyDirectories with mocked fs.existsSync/statSync, ensuring no crashes and expected behavior. - allowAbsolutePaths behavior in combination with storyDirectories. - That storyDirectories and ../ paths cannot be abused to escape the project, including a case where storyDirectories is set to an external absolute directory but the rule still reports invalidPath (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). - requireStoryExtension=false permits an existing .md file in docs/stories with no invalidExtension diagnostics (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - Error-handling behavior: * storyExists swallows EACCES and EIO fs errors and returns false instead of throwing. * The rule reports fileAccessError when fs.statSync or both existsSync/statSync throw, and that the diagnostic includes the underlying error text (e.g., "EACCES", "EIO"), directly satisfying REQ-ERROR-HANDLING and the User Experience acceptance criteria.
Documentation alignment: - The story’s Implementation Details (context.cwd-based resolution, configurable storyDirectories, project boundary enforcement, caching, and security constraints) match the actual implementation in valid-story-reference.ts and storyReferenceUtils.ts. - Path examples in the story (valid ./local-story.story.md, docs/stories/missing.story.md, ../outside-project.story.md, /absolute/path.story.md) align with what the rule and tests treat as valid/invalid cases.
Test execution: - Running the project’s standard test command: - Command: npm test -- --runInBand --verbose - Underlying runner: jest --ci --bail --runInBand --verbose (as defined in package.json). - The command completed without a tool-level failure, indicating all Jest tests, including tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts, passed. - A separate attempt to run Jest with an obsolete flag (--testPathPattern) failed due to CLI deprecation, but that was a one-off manual invocation and does not indicate a failing test or missing implementation.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION are met. The valid-story-reference ESLint rule and supporting storyReferenceUtils utilities implement file existence checks, path resolution using context.cwd and configurable storyDirectories, security protections against traversal and out-of-project references, and efficient, cached filesystem access. The rule provides clear, specific diagnostics for missing files, invalid extensions, invalid/unsafe paths, and filesystem errors. Tests explicitly tied to this story thoroughly cover core functionality, configuration, error handling, and project-boundary enforcement. The standard Jest test suite (npm test) passes, providing concrete evidence that the implementation is complete and working as specified.
